{"id":"01a10790-095b-76e2-a6b7-a1c0deaa8e86","created":true,"summary":"Invoice PDFs render via WeasyPrint in src/billing/pdf.py; font set by @font-face CSS in code (Inter, assets/Inter.woff2)"}

**What renders them:** `render_pdf()` in `src/billing/pdf.py` uses **WeasyPrint**. This is the v2 renderer. It's controlled by the `invoice-pdf-v2` flag, which is on in `flags.toml:3`. The old wkhtmltopdf renderer has been removed.

(A saved project note said fonts come from the container image and should be fixed in the Dockerfile. That only held while `invoice-pdf-v2` was off, so it no longer applies. I flagged that note and saved a corrected one.)

**Where to change the font:** in the `_STYLE` CSS block at `src/billing/pdf.py:8-11`:

```python
_STYLE = CSS(
    string="@font-face { font-family: Inter; src: url(assets/Inter.woff2); } body { font-family: Inter; }",
    font_config=_FONTS,
)
```

Change the `@font-face` source and the `body { font-family: ... }` value there.

**Likely cause of the wrong font:** the code asks for Inter, but there is no `Inter.woff2` (or any `Inter*` file) in the repo. The path `assets/Inter.woff2` is also relative, and neither `CSS(...)` nor `HTML(string=html)` gets a `base_url`, so it may not resolve even if the file exists. When WeasyPrint can't load an `@font-face` source, it falls back to a system font without raising an error. That matches what you're seeing. I only checked the repo, though; the font file might be added at build or deploy time.

To fix it:
1. Add the font file to the repo, e.g. `src/billing/assets/Inter.woff2`.
2. Point to it with an absolute path, e.g. `Path(__file__).parent / "assets" / "Inter.woff2"` as a `file://` URL, or pass `base_url=` to `CSS(...)`.
3. To confirm the font is failing to load, turn on WeasyPrint's logger (`weasyprint`) at WARNING level. It reports fonts it couldn't load.

I haven't changed any code. Do you want me to make this fix?
